hints: Split the original 15 bases C T A G A A T C C T C T C C C into five triplets from the left and use the table to find the five original amino acids. Count how many amino acids are coded for after the mutation.
A frameshift changes how all downstream triplets are grouped. Try deleting the third base A and regrouping the rest into new triplets CTA, AAT, CCT, CTC, then check them in the table.
walkthrough:
**Read the original code in triplets**

Start by grouping the original sequence from the left in threes. This is how the cell reads it.

$$CTA \; GAA \; TCC \; TCT \; CCC$$
Use the table with 1st base on the left and 2nd base on top. You get Asp, Leu, Arg, Arg, Gly. That is five amino acids.

**Notice what changed after mutation**

After mutation there are only four amino acids: Asp, Leu, Gly and Glu.
This tells you the reading frame must have shifted, because a simple substitution would still give five triplets. An insertion or deletion shifts every triplet after the mutation point.

**Test deletion of one nucleotide**

Delete the third base, the A in CTA:

$$C T [A] G A A T C C T C T C C C \rightarrow C T G A A T C C T C T C C C$$
Now regroup from the left:
$$CTG \; AAT \; CCT \; CTC$$
Check the table: CTG is Asp, AAT is Leu, CCT is Gly, CTC is Glu. This matches exactly Asp, Leu, Gly, Glu.

**Conclude the mutation type**

Only removing one base gives the correct new set of four amino acids by a frameshift. So the mutation was deletion of one nucleotide.

options.A: Correct. Deleting the A at position 3 shifts the frame to give CTG, AAT, CCT, CTC which code for Asp, Leu, Gly, Glu exactly.
options.B: False. Insertion of one base would give 16 bases and would not regroup to CTA/AAT type triplets that give Asp, Leu, Gly, Glu.
options.C: False. Insertion of two bases would give 17 bases and a different frameshift, it cannot produce the observed four triplets CTG, AAT, CCT, CTC.
options.D: False. Substitution of one base keeps 15 bases and five amino acids with no frameshift, so it cannot reduce the chain to four different amino acids.
